short_description: Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So Ada and her dog build, splash, blast off in a box rocket and bake. A funny bedtime picture book for ages 3–7, in paperback.
long_description:
The Day the Tablet Slept is a funny 32-page picture book for ages 3–7, in paperback. Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So what shall we do?

On Saturday morning, Ada zooms downstairs to find the family tablet snoring a teeny-tiny zzz-bip under a purple nightcap. It's taking a day off. So Ada and her dog Biscuit make their own fun. They build a block tower (CRASH!), splash through every puddle (SPLOOOSH, all over Papa), turn a big empty box into the ADA-1 rocket and blast off past a planet made entirely of socks. Then it's pancakes with Papa, a trip to the library's sleepy-story corner and a growly bear story at bedtime.

Children love to join in on the refrain, shout Biscuit's WOOF!, and check on the sleepy tablet as it snoozes through the day. Short, rhythmic read-aloud pages and bold, full-bleed pictures make it a cozy bedtime book and a fun one to read again and again. The tablet is never the bad guy. It just needed a nap, and in the morning Ada can't wait to tell it about her day.

At the back, grown-ups get 'Talk about it' questions, a 'Plan your own Play Day' page and a QR code for a free printable planner and coloring pages.

Pairs with 100 Screen-Free Plays as the Play Day bundle.
bullets: A funny bedtime story starring Ada, her dog Biscuit and a cardboard-box rocket, with a very sleepy tablet in a nightcap as the running joke
A read-aloud refrain ('Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So what shall we do?') and a WOOF! for children to shout along to

Bold, full-bleed flat illustrations on every spread, with a warm, varied cast (Papa is the everyday grown-up; Ms. Rosa the librarian wears glasses) and short, rhythmic pages that are easy to read aloud
Play ideas kids can copy right away: block towers, puddle jumping, a box rocket, cooking with a grown-up, a library visit and a bedtime story
Ends with open 'Talk about it' prompts (a sign, a point or a tap on a talker counts too), a 'Plan your own Play Day' point-and-pick page and a free printable bonus for grown-ups

launch_notes: Positioning: sell it as a funny bedtime and play-day story, not a screen-time book. Lead with Ada, Biscuit, the box rocket and the refrain in every listing, pin and ad. DEMAND-CHECK.md rates the category Weak and says not to count on this book alone, so its main job is to be the story half of the Play Day bundle. The hardcover file is ready, but per DEMAND-CHECK.md, turn on the IngramSpark hardcover only after the paperback shows sales. Printing costs nothing to hold, but the hardcover needs its own ISBN and a proof.
compliance_notes: No health or medical claims. The book is a story plus parent-education prompts and claims to treat, prevent or diagnose nothing. It is not presented as written by a speech-language pathologist. No diagnosis or condition terms anywhere in the book, listing or keywords (brand rule on condition searches). No research citations. No trademarked program names: the grown-up tips use plain words (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one word, follow their lead). No real brands, logos, devices, apps, schools or products: the tablet is a generic, unbranded character, and the copyright page says it is not based on any real product. Zero shame, zero preaching: every spread was checked. The tablet is never a villain or a warning. It takes a day off, the story never says screens are bad, and in the morning the tablet is welcomed back ('Wait till I tell you about my day…'). The 'Talk about it' prompts are open prompts with no right answers (days off, favorite parts, boxes, being Biscuit, cooking, and a calm crouch-and-stretch blast-off), not quiz questions or screen rules, and the grown-ups tip ends with 'Talk, sing and read in the language you know best. Every language counts.' (customer-voice rules 15 and 29). Every spread is 40 words or fewer (rule 30). No page asks a child to draw or write in the book (rule 44); the fill-in planner is the free printable. The book-within-the-book is an unnamed 'growly bear' book, not a real title. The copyright page carries 'Version 1.0 · September 2026' (rule 3); bump it on every change to a live file. Customer panel (panel.md, September 2026): the librarian no longer shushes (she welcomes Ada to the sleepy-story corner and waves), Ms. Rosa wears glasses (inclusive cast, rule 35), the grown-up tip adds a fill-in pause before 'do?' and 'A sign, a point or a tap on a talker counts too, and a talker never takes a day off' (rule 28), the sixth prompt is a calm blast-off movement, and the copyright page adds 'Grown-ups handle the stove, and everyone washes hands after cracking eggs.' Child safety: puddle play is shown with Papa, cooking with Papa handling the pan, and the box rocket is made from a big empty box and a marker. The copyright page says puddle play, cooking and box-building are best with a grown-up close by. No balloons, cords or choking-hazard foods appear. The copyright line follows legal/ENTITY.md: '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' The final logo from brand/logo/ (unaltered files) is on the front cover, the copyright page, the author-note page, the 'More from Play Before Pixels' page and the back cover, and the back cover carries a 'Read it, then play it' strip with playbeforepixels.com. Print notes: the PDFs are RGB. Chromium embeds the brand fonts as Type 3 fonts. KDP normally accepts both, but IngramSpark prefers PDF/X-1a in CMYK, so run its preflight and convert if it asks [VERIFY]. Check every file against the printer's current template before upload (KDP cover calculator, IngramSpark Cover Template Generator). KDP may print a manufacturing mark on the last page; page 32 keeps its bottom third clear (the 'More from' panel sits in the top two-thirds) [VERIFY]. Interior text sits at least 0.5 in inside the trim (IngramSpark's recommended safety area), and hardcover cover text sits at least 0.25 in inside the board edges. Picture books for ages 3–7 are generally treated as ordinary books under US CPSIA [VERIFY with the printer and CPSC guidance].
human_todo: HUMAN AUTHORSHIP (do this first): open WORDS.md and write, in your own words, the dedication (## dedication), 'A note from the author' (## note) and, if you want a credit, your name (## author). Pages 3 and 31 print as dashed 'Founder writes this page' boxes until you do. Then reread every story page aloud and rewrite any line in your own voice: names, jokes, the refrain, the order of events. Run the build commands in files.build_notes, and commit to git after each round so your changes are provable.

READ-ALOUD CHECK: read the whole book aloud three times, once at a tired bedtime pace, and fix any line that trips you. Keep every spread at 40 words or fewer and the refrain word-for-word the same (WORDS.md explains the markup). After any change to a file that is already on sale, bump VERSION in build.js ('Version 1.1 · Month Year') and tell past buyers what changed.

AI DISCLOSURE (honest answer for KDP): KDP asks whether the book has AI-generated text, images or translations. As built, the story text was drafted with AI (Claude) and the illustrations were drawn by AI-written code. Answer YES for AI-generated images, and YES for AI-generated text unless you have rewritten the text yourself. KDP counts AI-drafted text you later edited as AI-generated; only your own writing that you polished with AI counts as 'AI-assisted', which needs no disclosure. Give the same honest answer if IngramSpark or any store asks [VERIFY each platform's current wording]. If you register the copyright, claim only your own words and your selection and arrangement, and exclude the AI-generated material (see legal/protection/PROTECTION-PLAN.md).

ISBNs: buy your own ISBNs from Bowker (a block of 10 covers this and future books) so AlphaPlay LLC is listed as the publisher. The paperback and hardcover each need their own ISBN. A free KDP ISBN cannot be used at IngramSpark. Paste them into WORDS.md (## isbn-paperback, ## isbn-hardcover) so they print on the copyright page. Let KDP and IngramSpark place the barcode in the labelled 2 x 1.2 in box on the back cover, or place your own there.

KDP paperback: choose premium color, 8.5 x 8.5 in, bleed ON, glossy or matte cover. Upload picture-tablet-slept.pdf and cover-kdp-paperback.pdf. Check the spine width in KDP's cover calculator. If it differs from 0.0751 in, run KDP_SPINE_IN=<value> node build.js and re-render the cover PDF. Use the online previewer and fix every warning.

Download the template from the Cover Template Generator and compare it with cover-ingramspark-hardcover.pdf (0.625 in wrap, 0.5 in hinges, board = trim - 0.185 in wide and trim + 0.25 in tall). Rebuild with HC_SPINE_IN=<template spine> node build.js and re-render. Run their preflight, and convert to PDF/X-1a CMYK if asked [VERIFY].

Order a printed proof of each edition. Check the color (RGB to CMYK shift, especially the blue cover and the dark space and night spreads), the gutter, the trim, and whether the text reads easily. Confirm the QR code on page 30 scans.

A 32-page full-color story (12 spreads), 'Talk about it' prompts for grown-ups, a point-and-pick 'Plan your own Play Day' page and a QR code for a free printable planner and coloring pages.

faq.q: Is this a book about screen rules?
faq.a: No. It's a funny story about a day of play. The tablet is a friendly, sleepy character, and Ada can't wait to tell it about her day in the morning.
No, the story is print only. The Play Day planner and coloring pages are a free download from the QR code in the book.
Printing mistakes or damage are replaced by the store you bought from. See playbeforepixels.com for the full refund policy.

faq.q: My child talks with a tablet or device (a talker). Is this book a good fit?
faq.a: Yes. The sleepy tablet in the story is a made-up character, not a talker. The grown-up page says it plainly: a sign, a point or a tap on a talker counts, and a talker never takes a day off.
Yes. It's a funny read-aloud for ages 3–7 with a dedication page and a free printable planner to go with it. Order it with the recipient's address and use the store's gift options at checkout.

faq.q: Can I read it aloud at storytime or in class?
faq.a: Yes, reading the printed book aloud to a group in person is welcome. For a recorded or online read-aloud, ask first through the contact form at playbeforepixels.com.

faq.q: Can we order copies for a class, library or group?
faq.a: Yes. Use the quote form at playbeforepixels.com. Copies are printed on demand and shipped straight to you by the printer, with an emailed invoice.
Not yet. The book already says to talk, sing and read in the language you know best, and the sounds (WOOF!, zzz-bip) work in any language.
